description: We are Team Alpha 8, a group of developers turning complex NASA data into intuitive exploration tools. By combining deep GIS mapping expertise with creative web development, we are building a bridge between Earth and the stars. Our project transforms raw lunar topography and intimidating celestial physics into beautiful, real-time "Go/No-Go" landing navigators. We believe the journey to a permanent lunar base starts with understanding and we are here to make that data accessible to everyone.
summary:
Lunaritic is a lunar landing site analysis tool designed to identify safer and more suitable landing locations near the Moon’s poles. It analyzes environmental challenges such as sunlight availability, terrain features, and potential communication signal obstructions caused by mountains and craters. By visualizing and evaluating these conditions, the project helps researchers and mission planners make more informed decisions when selecting potential lunar landing sites.

The platform, officially named LUNARITIC (Lunar Navigation, Illumination & Risk Intelligence System), also includes interactive 3D lunar terrain visualization, landing-site comparison, sunlight and Earth visibility analysis, and mission planning tools.
details:
LUNARITIC is an interactive platform designed to identify safer and more suitable lunar landing sites, particularly near the Moon's poles. It analyzes terrain elevation, slope, surface roughness, sunlight availability, darkness duration, and Earth visibility using NASA datasets. Users can explore lunar terrain in 2D and 3D, compare potential landing locations, and evaluate mission conditions.

The project aims to make lunar mission planning safer, more efficient, and data-driven by combining multiple scientific factors in one platform. Its creativity lies in integrating terrain analysis, illumination, communication visibility, and landing-site scoring into a single interactive tool.

We developed it using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio, GDAL, and NASA's SPICE toolkit.

Our team considered landing safety, terrain conditions, sunlight availability, communication opportunities, mission timing, and scientific data accuracy.
